newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey scraps duty on petroleum sales for a month.
newsitem.headline: Turkey scraps duty on petroleum sales for a month.

text.p: Turkey abolished a 15-percent duty on retail sales of petroleum products for one month from March 15 in a test bid to see if refineries would benefit from the abolition, the Official Gazette said.
It said the duty, called Fuel Price Stabilisation Duty (AFIF), was scrapped for all grades of petrol, fuel-oil, diesel, gas oil, heating fuel, and liquefied petrolem gas (LPG).

Oil and refinery officials have said permanent abolition of the duty would be a major step in putting into practice a scheme called Automatic Pricing Mechanism (OFM), which they said was a a key prerequisite for the privatisation of Tupras, the state oil refinery.
They say OFM will also pave the way for the re-operation of Turkey's only private refinery, Atas, owned by the joint Mobil-British Petroleum partnership and Royal Dutch Shell.
Atas, which had a 14-percent market share, shut down its operation in October, saying AFIF and lack of the OFM had been inflicting losses which it said was about $55 million in 1996.
Officials said they might scrap AFIF for good depending on the results during the one-month abolition period.
Tupras said it raised retail prices of petroleum products as of Sunday by about seven percent because of currency differences.
